sites.trusted_source: caller identity token claims and allowed_tenants
sites.note: resolve_agora_user_scope distinguishes strict JWT authentication (token_kind == 'jwt' or PANTHEON_BFF_AUTH_MODE == 'strict') from non-strict stub mode. Under strict JWT auth, verified token claims are the sole authority: callers lacking tenant claims fail closed with 403 AGORA_SCOPE_TENANT_DENIED before any storage read or write. Configured environment defaults (PANTHEON_BFF_TENANT_ID, PANTHEON_BFF_DEFAULT_TENANT_ID, PANTHEON_TENANT_ID) and built-in fallback ('pantheon-dev') are never used as authenticated caller authority for tenantless callers, and requested_tenant_id is checked strictly against allowed_tenants. This centrally protects all Agora routes and stores including journal entries, performance suggestions & receipts, research dispatcher, and operational readiness.

Header/body tenant is requested_tenant_id into resolve_agora_user_scope which fails closed with 403 when caller identity lacks verified tenant claims in token; journal write handler also validates body tenant matches resolved caller tenant.

Operational readiness resolves scope via resolve_agora_user_scope. When caller presents tenantless signed JWT, scope resolution fails closed, setting scope=None. Under scope=None, private records are hidden and only public/shared records are returned. Mounted signed-JWT tests confirm zero disclosures of private tenant rows under built-in and active environment defaults, while same-tenant callers see their scoped private records.
